A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WeatherCity and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and all nine supplementary pages. The expanded references in v2 shift appendix pagination without creating gaps in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative and qualitative experiments on Waymo and nuScenes, including runtime measurements, ablations and supplementary comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Sections 4 and 7, including benchmark scores, ablations, temporal comparisons and the ClimateNeRF comparison.

M1.justification: The Qwen-based editing, shared Gaussian features, weather-specific decoders, losses and weather simulation procedures are unchanged. The shortened content-loss description retains the same raw-image target in Equation 7.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Waymo and nuScenes coverage for rain, snow and fog editing, temporal consistency and object manipulation. No training or evaluation domain or task is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments: ControlNet, TurboEdit, FRESCO, Qwen-Image and the supplementary ClimateNeRF comparison. WeatherEdit and Weather-Magician are newly discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The five-scene, 30-frame evaluation description, image resolutions, training settings, prompts and runtime procedures are retained. Metrics are unchanged, including evaluating fog only with CLIP-DS in the supplement.

E4.justification: The Gaussian-representation and content-loss ablations, dynamic-weather comparison with Qwen-Image, object-editing examples and supplementary temporal analyses are retained without new or revised tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The reporting of point estimates remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and 5–7 and the qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, WeatherCity retains Waymo scores of 0.872/0.303/0.915 in Table 1 and a rendering speed of 25.67 FPS.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16 retain the same Gaussian definitions, rendering expressions, losses, motion models and metric formulas. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about unified 4D reconstruction, consistent weather editing and physics-driven simulation. Added table-caption statements repeat existing performance claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the ablations, temporal consistency and depth-aware effects remain unchanged. The manual particle-tuning limitation and the qualification about content-preservation metrics under fog are retained; the limitations paragraph merely moves onto page 8.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release statement and repository link to the abstract. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and supplementary instructions are unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access pointer, not the repository's actual availability or contents.

R1.justification: Six references are added, including WeatherEdit and Weather-Magician. Sections 1 and 2.3 newly distinguish WeatherCity's cross-weather consistency from WeatherEdit's independent reconstructions. Let it Snow was already cited in v1; its revised title does not represent another added work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits, expands the affiliation, revises author footnotes, adds acknowledgements and updates bibliographic details. The main section structure and supplementary narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 and Table 3 gain explanatory caption text, with adjustments to table spacing and page layout. All 17 figures and seven tables are retained; figure image contents are unchanged, and the supplement shifts after the expanded references.

improvement.justification: The added discussion of closely related weather-editing methods improves research positioning, while the code-release pointer improves access documentation. These are limited gains: the method, experimental evidence and limitations remain unchanged, and code availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.
